scores.scale: 0 unusable; 5 workable with substantial friction; 7 good with noticeable friction; 10 exceptional clarity, control and consistency across assessed content. Scores are subjective observations of these two assisted, paused emulation attempts, not a completion grade or physical-device certification.

reasons.overall_mobile: Accessible route/tap assistance and coherent objective feedback supported a complete mission, while dense controls, divided attention and costly stationary combat limited comfort.
reasons.controls: Tap aim, TURN and simultaneous route/fire worked. Layout is crowded; manual precision movement and aiming remain untested.
reasons.gameplay: Memory-to-coil-to-upload progression and timing/resource consequences were understandable; shorter bursts gave a meaningful improvement. Threat management during coil windows was taxing.
reasons.presentation: Strong consistent industrial atmosphere and cyan/amber identity in observed scenes; audio and physical motion/performance unassessed.
reasons.usability: Concise handbook, paused planning and clear terminal choices helped. Timing/defense and several simultaneous HUD demands add learning friction.
reasons.readability: Primary health, ammo, objective, OFF and upload status readable; secondary uppercase telemetry and map details small.

helpful: Readable initial mobile handbook explains movement, tap aim, route hold, coil windows and deck upload in one screen
Tap aim and hold FIRE killed the opening guard without fine thumb precision
HOLD ROUTE traversed the facility and recovered receivers, reducing navigation burden
Numbered memory tiles and coil OFF status made progress visible
Both terminal screens fit portrait and clearly separated START FRESH from checkpoint retry
frustrating: At 390px wide, controls occupy much of the lower view; FIRE/AIM/RELOAD/DASH/JUMP/ROUTE/TOOLS and TURN create a dense attention area
Stationary coil firing caused a steep health/ammo penalty; first attempt reached return with 16 health and zero reserve, then died
Boss status and offscreen threat cue compete for attention; a clear warning still requires interrupting another task
Small uppercase secondary HUD text, fine map legend and dense terminal telemetry need deliberate inspection
presentation: Consistent cyan/amber visual language, industrial rain scene, receiver signage and restrained typography gave a coherent atmosphere
Dark geometry and some thin labels reduced immediate legibility; screenshots alone do not establish motion quality
